newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian police say designer drug could be deadly.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian police say designer drug could be deadly.

text.p: Australian police warned on Monday that a potent new drug cocktail that left nine young people in intensive care after a weekend party could prove fatal next time around.
The nine all collapsed on Sunday morning after an all-night party on the eastern Gold Coast and were rushed to intensive care units. Some had stopped breathing.
A Queensland police statement on Monday said seven of them were still in hospital "in a serious but stable condition",
"Senior police warn the next victims of the designer drug, dubbed a 'cocktail of death', may not survive," the statement added.
The nine, six men and three women in their mid-20s, were said to have mixed the drug with soft drink and water to reduce its potency, swallowing a mouthful of the mixture each.
Police were still analysing samples of the drug but said it appeared to be "Gamma Hydroxybutic Acid" or GHB, a hallucinogenic chemical drug that causes comas.
It is better known in Britain -- from where it may have come -- as GBH or "Grievous Bodily Harm".
Acting Superintendent Peter Barron of the Queensland drug investigation squad said it was possible the drug was supplied either from abroad or from elsewhere in Australia.
Barron warned that the GHB could return during the Gold Coast's "Schoolies Week" in November, when students celebrate the end of their school year.
"Unfortunately, we cannot stop anybody from taking these drugs and the Gold Coast incident is a blatant warning to all parents and teenagers," Barron said.
